overall: The AG found the committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently detailed April 30 notice that omitted the anticipated Nash School closure topic, but not intentionally. Other allegations were not substantiated.

allegations.summary: Budget subcommittee allegedly deliberated on closing a school on April 28 or 29 without a posted meeting; complainant offered no further specifics.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Mr. Mackin’s allegation was not sufficiently specific, nor did he provide any subsequent details, which would enable us to further investigate this allegation.

allegations.summary: The April 30 meeting notice listed only a general budget-submission topic, not the possible closure of a specific school that was anticipated to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting by posting an insufficiently detailed meeting notice for its April 30 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the insufficient April 30 notice was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, we do not find that the Committee acted intentionally to violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A quorum of the committee allegedly deliberated at a superintendent-hosted open forum on May 6 without posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find here that the Committee did not deliberate where the comments made by Chair Belmarsh and Mr. Sullivan were directed to the public to provide information and answers, and were not directed at each other or the other members of the Committee present at the open forum.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements (no civil penalty; the committee was warned that a future notice violation could be evidence of intent and could draw a civil penalty up to $1,000 per occurrence).
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
